description: SB1-oriented rule catalog. Transferred VC5 rules are hypotheses until validated with Speedy Blupi evidence. No runtime dependency on blood2_recon.

rules.title: A repeated field read may mean the source had no cached local
rules.symptom: Native reloads a member chain; ours keeps one value live.
rules.construct: Repeated member expression versus one named pointer/value local.
rules.explanation: VC5 may reload across calls or aliasing stores instead of keeping an optimizer-created cache.
rules.experiment: Remove the local and restore the full member expression at each native read.
rules.not_when: Do not do this when native reads once and reuses the value.

rules.title: A value read once may have had a named local
rules.symptom: Native loads a value once and reuses its register; ours reloads it.
rules.construct: One local holding a field, call result, list head, or repeated size.
rules.explanation: A local forces one evaluation where an intervening call/store may alias.
rules.experiment: Introduce one local at the likely original declaration point and reuse it.
rules.not_when: Avoid when VC5 already reuses the cheap expression.

rules.title: Block scope can reuse dead stack slots
rules.symptom: Stack offsets or frame size differ while the main instruction shape is close.
rules.construct: Place a local inside its use block or at function scope.
rules.explanation: VC5 may assign inner-block locals to slots whose prior values are dead.
rules.experiment: Compare the evidenced scope and declaration lifetime; inspect debug output if available.
rules.not_when: This does not explain a register-only difference.
rules.keywords: scope stack slot frame local lifetime

rules.title: Local declaration order is usually inert
rules.symptom: Only local slot order or SIB operand order differs.
rules.construct: Swap adjacent local declarations.
rules.explanation: Corpus results show declaration swaps rarely alter optimized code.
rules.experiment: Try one evidence-backed order only after checking TU context.
rules.not_when: Do not permute declarations broadly.

rules.title: Independent statements can preserve native store order
rules.symptom: The same operations appear in a different order.
rules.construct: Order independent assignments as they appear in native.
rules.explanation: VC5 commonly retains source statement order at /O2.
rules.experiment: Reorder one semantics-independent pair and compare the whole TU.
rules.not_when: Check flags and dependencies before reordering.

blupi_evidence.outcome: A register-only ECX/EDX residue was NOT moved by top/before count probes 0-64 but was fixed by writing pos.x before pos.y; identical prefix grew 3,381 -> 4,886 bytes.

rules.title: /O1 can move stores that /O2 leaves in source order
rules.symptom: /O1 and /O2 disagree on independent store order.
rules.construct: Keep the source order evidenced by the /O2 target.
rules.explanation: The size-oriented path can schedule independent stores differently.
rules.experiment: Confirm the owning TU flags before changing source.
rules.not_when: Do not apply from a single image without flag evidence.

rules.title: A call comparison and a local comparison can use different boolean code
rules.symptom: Native uses neg/sbb while ours uses test/setcc, or the reverse.
rules.construct: Compare the call expression directly versus a local holding its result.
rules.explanation: VC5 selects a different boolean idiom from these source forms.
rules.experiment: Compile both forms with the real return type.
rules.not_when: Check byte versus integer return width first.

rules.title: Result width selects byte or dword instructions
rules.symptom: Native uses AL while ours uses EAX, or movsx differs from movzx.
rules.construct: Match the declared return or member width and signedness.
rules.explanation: The prototype and member types control extension and result width.
rules.experiment: Check the shared declaration before changing the caller.
rules.not_when: Do not override a fixed SDK prototype.

blupi_evidence.outcome: char-return candidate emitted 32 bytes and mismatched; int __cdecl candidate matched the 34-byte target body in a 48-byte COFF window

rules.title: VC5 folds within an expression but keeps some statement boundaries
rules.symptom: Native performs two constant operations; ours combines them, or vice versa.
rules.construct: Split or merge arithmetic at the evidenced local/statement boundary.
rules.explanation: Expression folding does not necessarily cross a stored local.
rules.experiment: Compile the two minimal source forms at the same function site.
rules.not_when: A genuinely wrong constant is a source difference.

rules.title: Branch layout often follows source block order
rules.symptom: Equivalent blocks appear in another order or conditional polarity.
rules.construct: Restore the native then/else ordering and condition shape.
rules.explanation: VC5 commonly emits the source then-block first.
rules.experiment: Compare one condition/body rearrangement at the same flags.
rules.not_when: Do not invert semantics based only on address layout.

blupi_evidence.outcome: zero-dimension test before clamp changed branch layout and produced a strict 108-byte target body

rules.title: Destructor scopes can distinguish fall-through from early return
rules.symptom: Native branches to a destructor test; ours returns to the epilogue.
rules.construct: A scoped fall-through block versus an early return.
rules.explanation: A live destructor joins cleanup paths differently.
rules.experiment: Restore the source scope/exit form supported by object lifetime evidence.
rules.not_when: Trivial locals may not show this effect.

rules.title: Several guards can differ from one joined exit
rules.symptom: Native has distinct guard exits; ours joins them into one path.
rules.construct: Separate guard returns versus a shared final return.
rules.explanation: VC5 preserves different exit structures when cleanup and branch joins differ.
rules.experiment: Try only the guard structure indicated by native control flow.
rules.not_when: Check destructor scope and conditions first.

blupi_evidence.outcome: Target-based helicopter guard and creature/player-position skip plus uninitialized IntersectRect output changed a 512-byte baseline candidate to 608 bytes; target body is 538 bytes and remains MISMATCH. A short type local had no further code-size effect; negative only for these tested source forms.

rules.title: Inline decisions can vary by caller site
rules.symptom: The same helper is called at some sites and expanded at others.
rules.construct: Restore the real helper call sites and wrapper layers.
rules.explanation: VC5 spends a caller-local inline budget; expansion size and nesting matter.
rules.experiment: List calls in source order and test one caller with the real helper body.
rules.not_when: Do not add inline/noinline hints to force a call list.

rules.title: Expanded wrappers can add later inline decisions
rules.symptom: Nested helper calls expand at sites with an unexpected order.
rules.construct: Restore an evidenced wrapper call instead of direct calls.
rules.explanation: Nested sites may be considered after direct sites and in reverse order.
rules.experiment: Compare direct and wrapper forms in one caller.
rules.not_when: The observed order is VC5-specific and bounded.

rules.title: Call a real inline member instead of open-coding it
rules.symptom: A helper body is expanded but register or load choices differ.
rules.construct: Use the original helper call expression when its definition is available.
rules.explanation: Inline-body source context can affect the generated sequence.
rules.experiment: Compare one call site against the open-coded body.
rules.not_when: Do not invent a helper absent from source evidence.

rules.title: /O1 can leave larger inline bodies out of line
rules.symptom: Helper calls differ between /O1 and /O2.
rules.construct: Use the actual per-TU optimization level.
rules.explanation: VC5 /O1 and /O2 can choose different inline shapes.
rules.experiment: Compile both authentic flag sets before changing helper source.
rules.not_when: Do not transfer a project-wide flag assumption to every TU.

rules.title: Register-only residues may come from TU-wide compiler context
rules.symptom: Instruction shape is stable but registers or commutative operands differ.
rules.construct: Test authentic TU context before rewriting expressions.
rules.explanation: A TU symbol counter can select among equal-cost code sequences.
rules.experiment: Use count probes at top, end, and before the function on scratch copies.
rules.not_when: A probe is diagnostic only; never keep artificial declarations.
rules.keywords: symbol counter register x87 SIB TU

blupi_evidence.tu: button.cpp; sound.h included before member bodies
blupi_evidence.outcome: SB1 SP3 count probes: top and before:MouseMove restore STRICT at counts 7-14 and 23-30; end probes do not restore through count 32. Pre-function declaration context is measured; exact counter phase is inferred from placement response. SB1 confirmation incl. resolution by genuine declarations: see BLUPI-CTX-01.

rules.title: An earlier source change can move a later function
rules.symptom: A nearby edit changes another function without changing its semantics.
rules.construct: Compare cross-function effects after each source edit.
rules.explanation: Compiler numbering and phase context can couple functions in one TU.
rules.experiment: Record the strict status vector for the full TU, not one function.
rules.not_when: Do not attribute every peer change to source semantics.

blupi_evidence.outcome: Across baseline, StopSound-only, and SB2-header full builds (9 TUs each), adding BOOL CSound::StopSound(int) changed accepted peers in button.cpp and menu.cpp; the StopSound-only candidate made all three STRICT baselines MISMATCH. SB1 confirmation incl. resolution by genuine declarations: see BLUPI-CTX-01.

rules.title: Probe placement can separate TU context hypotheses
rules.symptom: Top/end/before-function probes affect different later regions.
rules.construct: Compare the same count at three scratch-only insertion points.
rules.explanation: Different placement responses can reveal local versus delayed compiler work.
rules.experiment: Use small counts and compare all peer functions.
rules.not_when: No response in a bounded range does not disprove all context effects.
rules.keywords: count probe top end before function

blupi_evidence.tu: button.cpp; probes at top, before:MouseMove, and end
blupi_evidence.outcome: Counts 7-14 and 23-30 at top/before restore STRICT; no end placement from 0 through 32 does. Placement localizes the measured sensitivity to context preceding MouseMove, with phase attribution remaining an inference.

rules.title: A strict gain in one function can break a peer
rules.symptom: A source edit helps one function but shifts another.
rules.construct: Keep the full translation-unit strict result beside the target result.
rules.explanation: Shared TU context and data bindings couple otherwise separate bodies.
rules.experiment: Recompare every function after each successful edit.
rules.not_when: Do not promote a target-only gain without peer review.

blupi_evidence.outcome: The 99-byte StopSound body at 0x23050 is STRICT (candidate object emits 112 bytes including 13 trailing NOPs); adding its declaration changes three accepted peer bodies from STRICT to MISMATCH in the StopSound-only full build.

rules.title: Automatic PCH mode is part of the build context
rules.symptom: A broad TU difference appears with /YX or include order.
rules.construct: Match the original IDE PCH settings and creation order.
rules.explanation: Automatic precompiled headers alter the compiler input stream.
rules.experiment: Compare with and without the authentic PCH procedure.
rules.not_when: Do not treat /YX as a generic speed flag.

rules.title: Definition order can affect delayed compiler work
rules.symptom: Later functions shift after a definition or template moves.
rules.construct: Restore the evidenced definition order in the owning TU.
rules.explanation: Some VC5 work is deferred until later in the translation unit.
rules.experiment: Move only a real definition supported by source evidence.
rules.not_when: Do not add dummy definitions for alignment.

rules.title: Commutative x87 order can be TU context
rules.symptom: Only the x87 operand load/reverse sequence differs.
rules.construct: Check TU context before swapping source operands.
rules.explanation: VC5 can choose x87 operand order from a numbered tie-break.
rules.experiment: Try a bounded scratch count probe before changing the expression.
rules.not_when: Keep noncommutative floating operations semantically fixed.

rules.title: Test a flag on the target function, not by its name
rules.symptom: A flag change is proposed to explain a local instruction difference.
rules.construct: Change one compiler flag while holding source and context fixed.
rules.explanation: Option names do not predict which target body will improve.
rules.experiment: Compare the target and every peer under authentic settings.
rules.not_when: Do not globally promote a flag from one function.

rules.title: Compiler package effects can vary by TU
rules.symptom: One function agrees across builds but a peer changes.
rules.construct: Sweep compiler builds on the owning TU with headers fixed.
rules.explanation: Front-end context and compiler package can interact.
rules.experiment: Compare per-function bytes and isolate compiler components before attribution.
rules.not_when: Do not call packages interchangeable from one helper.

rules.title: C++ unwind paths require the matching EH flag
rules.symptom: Cleanup calls or exception frames are missing.
rules.construct: Match /GX, then recover real C++ scopes and destructors.
rules.explanation: VC5 /GX enables the measured C++ unwind support.
rules.experiment: Compile a minimal throwing call with a destructor and inspect the object.
rules.not_when: Function-body bytes alone omit some EH sections.

rules.title: Intrinsic calls can change with optimization mode
rules.symptom: memcpy/memset calls appear in one optimization mode but not another.
rules.construct: Use the source construct and authentic /O1 or /O2 setting.
rules.explanation: VC5 may call these intrinsics at /O1 and expand them at /O2.
rules.experiment: Compile both real flag sets and compare peer functions.
rules.not_when: Do not infer the source helper from the call alone.

rules.title: Constant, condition, and offset differences usually mean real source differences
rules.symptom: A value, branch condition, or memory displacement differs.
rules.construct: Check literal values, comparison operators, prototypes, and field layout.
rules.explanation: VC5 preserves many semantic differences rather than normalizing them.
rules.experiment: Trace the value or offset to source/header evidence before codegen experiments.
rules.not_when: Register-only and reorder-only diffs need a different first step.

evidence.counts: CurrentWrite STRICT at 0x14da0 (1,574 target bytes; 14 relocations) after a contiguous start-direction memcpy and signed int fwrite test; CurrentRead and FileExist cleanup variants remain mismatches.

blupi_evidence.outcome: Inherited int result accumulator plus else-if mismatched; private void declaration plus independent start/end checks emitted 128 COFF bytes and strictly matched the 115-byte target. The source changes were tested together.

rules.title: Many equivalent spellings produce identical code
rules.symptom: A syntax-only rewrite is proposed with no instruction evidence.
rules.construct: Avoid changing equivalent boolean, increment, or pointer spellings by default.
rules.explanation: VC5 normalizes many such forms; corpus perturbations were usually inert.
rules.experiment: Spend compiles on a source form that predicts a visible instruction change.
rules.not_when: A type, alias, or statement-boundary change is not merely spelling.
rules.keywords: inert equivalent spelling do not try

rules.title: Commuting arithmetic and expanding compound assignment are usually inert
rules.symptom: Only arithmetic operand order or compound-assignment spelling differs.
rules.construct: Do not try these as a byte-matching lever without evidence.
rules.explanation: Measured VC5 corpus perturbations rarely changed the output.
rules.experiment: Move to a different hypothesis after one inert check.
rules.not_when: This does not cover changed types or side effects.

rules.title: Dummy declarations are not a source reconstruction
rules.symptom: Padding declarations are proposed to reach another code shape.
rules.construct: Use counter declarations only in scratch diagnostics.
rules.explanation: A probe response says nothing about whether the original contained padding.
rules.experiment: Remove probes before candidate source is promoted.
rules.not_when: Never use artificial code in canonical matching sources.

rules.title: OutputDebug calls fold to the empty menu destructor
rules.symptom: Many calls resolve to a one-byte ret at RVA 0x1f010.
rules.construct: The empty CMenu destructor is emitted in menu.cpp with /Gy COMDAT packaging.
rules.explanation: The SB1 linker folds identical eligible COMDAT bodies; call targets can name the destructor-owned ret. The verifier reports FOLDED separately from STRICT.
rules.experiment: Compare object sections and call relocations, then verify the folded owner and RVA in the linked image.
rules.not_when: This is linker placement evidence, not a compiler-function match.

evidence.counts: 56 OutputDebug call sites; target RVA 0x1f010; five-TU comparison

rules.keywords: COMDAT folding FOLDED OutputDebug ret destructor linker

blupi_evidence.outcome: 56 calls resolve to the destructor-owned bare ret; comparator models FOLDED

rules.title: RTM changes two SB1 sound helpers under fixed SP3 headers
rules.symptom: RTM and SP3 bodies differ in two sound helpers although the selected target stays strict.
rules.construct: Same sound TU, fixed headers, flags, oracle and link context; change compiler tree.
rules.explanation: SB1 evidence rejects universal VC5-build interchangeability. The RTM cause is not isolated to c1xx or c2.
rules.experiment: Compare both helpers and all TU peers; isolate compiler components before attribution.
rules.not_when: Do not infer that every RTM function differs.

evidence.counts: 36 compiles; CreateSoundBuffer 23 fixed bytes; ReadData 232 fixed bytes

blupi_evidence.outcome: RTM differs in 23 and 232 non-relocated bytes; target remains STRICT

rules.title: __FILE__ and __LINE__ are observable SB1 inputs
rules.symptom: A path string or diagnostic line argument differs even when surrounding logic matches.
rules.construct: TRY_DS passes __FILE__ and __LINE__; VC5 embeds the source path and line values.
rules.explanation: The oracle contains F:\Profil\sound.cpp; a local absolute or relative source path emits a different literal. Line shifts can change diagnostic arguments.
rules.experiment: Keep source line numbering and compile path stable; inspect the data relocation and argument pushes.
rules.not_when: Do not mask string/data differences as codegen noise.

evidence.counts: F:\Profil\sound.cpp at RVA 0x7b484; TraceErrorDS strict at RVA 0x1ffa0

blupi_evidence.outcome: source path is byte-visible; TRY_DS line numbers remain preserved in the candidate

rules.title: Treat decompiler prototypes and merged control flow as hypotheses
rules.symptom: Pseudocode suggests a different prototype, merged branch, or guessed field name.
rules.construct: Translate instructions, call targets and field offsets into a minimal source candidate; compile and compare.
rules.explanation: The SB1 pilot found useful body/call structure but unreliable inferred parameters, return widths, and field names.
rules.experiment: Check prototypes from ret/stack behavior, then compile the smallest semantic source form and use strict cmpfunc verification.
rules.not_when: Pseudocode similarity is not evidence of source identity.

evidence.counts: 7 targeted compiles; 5/6 selected functions strict after translation and relocation proof; ChangeSprite remained mismatch

rules.keywords: decompiler Ghidra prototype calling convention field offset branch ChangeSprite

blupi_evidence.function: ChangeSprite; CEvent::FlushInput; CButton::TreatEvent; CMenu::TreatEvent; two wrappers
blupi_evidence.outcome: instruction-led translation resolved five selected cases; ChangeSprite still differs

rules.title: Caching the PlaySoundDS member pointer did not improve the SB1 match
rules.symptom: A cached member pointer changes the body but leaves PlaySoundDS mismatching.
rules.construct: Load m_lpDSB[dwSound] once into a typed local, then use the local across the existing calls.
rules.explanation: The one tested cache changed output size without matching the oracle or improving the strict peer count.
rules.experiment: Do not repeat this cache form without new evidence of a value-lifetime mismatch; test the direct member reads first.
rules.not_when: This is one SB1 function and one candidate form, not a general rule against local caching.

evidence.counts: 1 candidate compile; body 128 -> 112 bytes; zero wildcard hits; 21/27 strict peers unchanged

rules.keywords: PlaySoundDS cached pointer local member reload negative no strict gain

blupi_evidence.outcome: 128-byte baseline -> 112-byte cached form; MISMATCH, zero wildcard hits; 21/27 strict peers unchanged

rules.title: CPixmap has a measured four-byte slot at this+8
rules.symptom: A CPixmap-like body differs in field offsets and load/call structure.
rules.construct: Keep a neutral BOOL member at offset +8 after m_mouseType; initialize it in the constructor.
rules.explanation: Target code writes and reads this slot; adding it shifts later members by four bytes. Its semantic name is unknown.
rules.experiment: Check constructor and method offsets, then compile the full pixmap TU and compare all peers strictly.
rules.not_when: Do not infer a semantic field name from the offset or apply this layout to another class.

evidence.counts: Four CPixmap candidate object variants; final isolated TU: 20 STRICT, 4 RELOC-UNVERIFIED, 21 MISMATCH; Create remains mismatched

rules.keywords: CPixmap offset layout m_unknown08 field structure class member

blupi_evidence.function: CPixmap constructor; CPixmap::Create and other field users
blupi_evidence.outcome: slot at +8 required to align later target fields; 20/45 strict cluster functions, target Create still MISMATCH

rules.title: CJauge::Draw passes channel id 5 in the oracle
rules.symptom: The source candidate pushes 12 twice where the oracle pushes 5.
rules.construct: Set the scratch UI header CHJAUGE value to 5 for CJauge::Draw.
rules.explanation: The value is an SB1 channel identifier from the target body. This does not establish the correct value for other builds or projects.
rules.experiment: Compile the owning TU with the candidate value and strict-verify it; inspect remaining call relocations before claiming equality.
rules.not_when: Do not change the canonical source from this one function result without verifying the owning header and all users.

evidence.counts: Five candidate compiler invocations; Draw moved from MISMATCH to RELOC-UNVERIFIED after the two immediate operands changed; three DrawPart REL32 targets unresolved

rules.keywords: CJauge Draw CHJAUGE channel id constant immediate 5 12 ?Draw@CJauge@@QAEXXZ

blupi_evidence.outcome: oracle pushes 5 twice; value-5 candidate moved Draw to RELOC-UNVERIFIED, not STRICT; three DrawPart REL32 targets lack unique verified RVAs

rules.title: CDecor FIFO fields precede no-barre and timers
rules.symptom: BlupiAddFifo accesses the FIFO count and positions below their SB2-derived offsets.
rules.construct: Place m_blupiFifoNb and m_blupiFifoPos[10] after m_blupiDynamite and before m_blupiNoBarre and the timer fields in the private CDecor layout.
rules.explanation: The target uses offsets +0xc978 and +0xc97c; moving the fields by -0x1c aligns the candidate accesses.
rules.experiment: Compile the full decblupi candidate after changing only private member order.
rules.not_when: Do not promote the scratch layout to shared headers before all dependent TUs are reconciled.

evidence.counts: VC5 SP3; BlupiAddFifo became STRICT for 142 target bytes after a -0x1c field shift

blupi_evidence.outcome: FIFO field order shifted accesses by -0x1c and produced a strict body; private layout only

rules.title: CDecor power flag precedes shield flag
rules.symptom: CaisseGetMove reads m_blupiPower four bytes after the target access.
rules.construct: Declare m_blupiPower before m_blupiShield in the private CDecor layout.
rules.explanation: The target reads Power at +0xc934; placing Power before Shield shifts it four bytes to that offset.
rules.experiment: Compile the full decmove candidate after changing only private member order.
rules.not_when: Do not infer unrelated field order from this single target access.

evidence.counts: VC5 SP3; CaisseGetMove became STRICT for 89 target bytes after a four-byte field shift

blupi_evidence.outcome: Power field shifted by -4 bytes and produced a strict body; private layout only

rules.title: Benchmark uses the SB1 ten-frame average and output
rules.symptom: The inherited SB2 benchmark reports memory and raw elapsed time instead of the SB1 average and log text.
rules.construct: Count down ten UpdateFrame/SetDecor/Display iterations, handle the millisecond wrap, divide elapsed milliseconds by ten, and emit the SB1 CheckTime line to data\time.blp.
rules.explanation: The target pseudocode and embedded strings identify the SB1 benchmark behavior. The corrected scratch TU compares STRICT; this is a game-version source difference.
rules.experiment: Compile the owning blupi.cpp TU with VC5 SP3 and compare the full function at RVA 0x1d60, including every relocation.
rules.not_when: Do not transfer the output string, file behavior, or timing calculation to another build without target evidence.

evidence.counts: Final SP3 candidate: 208-byte span STRICT at 0x1d60 against a 204-byte Ghidra body; all relocations proven.

rules.keywords: Benchmark time average ten frames CheckTime time.blp SB1 source behavior

blupi_evidence.outcome: SB1 loop, average, and output behavior compare STRICT; 208-byte candidate span covers 204-byte target body.

rules.title: SetDecor passes the mouse point with the build rectangle
rules.symptom: The target Build call site includes the rectangle and two additional point words.
rules.construct: Pass posMouse as the second value to the private CDecor::Build(RECT, POINT) declaration.
rules.explanation: The candidate without the point argument mismatched. Adding it produced the exact caller bytes and relocation to the Build entry at 0x404350; the target callee returns with ret 0x18.
rules.experiment: Compile the owning blupi.cpp TU and compare SetDecor at RVA 0x14f0, explicitly mapping Build to VA 0x404350.
rules.not_when: This evidence is limited to the SB1 SetDecor call and the matching private header. Do not change other Build call sites without their target evidence.

evidence.counts: Build(RECT) was MISMATCH; Build(RECT, POINT) produced a 208-byte STRICT span at 0x14f0 with the Build relocation proven.

rules.keywords: SetDecor CDecor Build RECT POINT call arguments stack cleanup source header

blupi_evidence.outcome: Adding the POINT argument changed the callsite to STRICT; target Build entry ends with ret 0x18.

rules.title: Incomplete shared-header declarations shift VC5 TU context of including files
rules.symptom: Adding the real StopSound declaration changes MouseMove and other accepted functions in TUs that include sound.h.
rules.construct: Recover the authentic declaration set and order from SB1 evidence; compare all peers after each header change.
rules.explanation: Under the pinned SP3 build, MouseMove responds to pre-function count context in two bounded windows, while end-of-TU probes do not. A strict StopSound body therefore does not establish a safe header context.
rules.experiment: Compile all accepted functions with baseline and real-declaration-only scratch headers; use top/before/end probes diagnostically, then remove them.
rules.not_when: Never keep filler declarations to land in a probe window; the probe only shows that the original had a different preceding declaration count - find the real declarations (here: unreconstructed helper methods of the same class).

evidence.counts: 99 count-probe compiles; 27 full-TU builds across baseline, StopSound-only, and SB2-header contexts; 3 accepted peer regressions

Resolution: real SB1 declarations for the sound helpers (PlaySoundDS(int,int,int,int) 0x22f00, PlaySoundDS(int,int,int) 0x22fc0, PlayImage 0x230c0, Play 0x23220) make StopSound STRICT while CButton::TreatEvent, CButton::MouseMove and CMenu::TreatEvent stay STRICT (copied-tree all-TU build).

Second instance: six declarations gated per TU regressed CButton::MouseMove when unguarded; completing all SB1 class declarations (full method inventories in plausible order) made them unconditional with MouseMove still STRICT (317/318 accepted). Remaining GetBlupiInfo window +24..27/+32 top/before only -> missing preceding decblock bodies.

rules.keywords: sound.h declaration count MouseMove StopSound peer regression

blupi_evidence.tu: sound.cpp; button.cpp and menu.cpp include sound.h
blupi_evidence.outcome: StopSound is STRICT, but StopSound-only and SB2-header candidates break accepted peers. Pre-function probes restore MouseMove at counts 7-14 and 23-30; end probes do not through 32. No original header context is established. RESOLVED (coreres round): the missing genuine helper declarations, not fillers, restored the original context; all four functions STRICT together.

rules.title: Local arrays: function-scope arrays are laid out by ascending size; sibling-block arrays share one slot
rules.symptom: Stack displacements of local buffers differ (e.g. [esp+0x10c] vs [esp+0xa8]) although frame size matches.
rules.construct: Which scope each array is declared in, and which arrays live in disjoint sibling blocks.
rules.explanation: VC5 SP3 /O2 /GX (35 isolated probes): function-scope arrays are placed in ascending size order independent of declaration or first-use order; arrays declared in sibling blocks/cases share one slot sized to the largest; small (12/28-byte) arrays keep separate slots; passing an address or using a struct of equal size does not move a slot; a destructor in a throwing try adds a 4-byte slot.
rules.experiment: Map every target [esp+N] buffer to a source variable; group them into ascending runs; each run is one scope level (function scope first, then inner block groups); declare buffers accordingly and recompile.
rules.not_when: Scalar spills and register-allocated locals follow other rules; the rule is measured on VC5 SP3 /O2 only and inner-block group ordering is still a hypothesis.
rules.keywords: stack slot local array buffer layout ascending size scope block share frame

blupi_evidence.function: CEvent::ChangePhase (target map consistent with function-scope ascending run + inner block run)
blupi_evidence.outcome: Rule measured in micro TUs; application to ChangePhase pending

rules.title: A SIB base/index swap can be caused by the control-flow shape of another block in the same function
rules.symptom: Same effective address, SIB base and index registers swapped, early in a large function; equivalent address spellings do not change it.
rules.construct: Shape of other blocks in the same function (switch vs if-chain, block order), not the address expression itself.
rules.explanation: VC5 allocates registers function-wide; changing a later block's control-flow shape changed which register became base/index in an earlier loop. Wide TU count probes (end 0-64 step 1, 64-512 step 16; top/before 0-64) never flipped it, so it was not TU context here.
rules.experiment: After 2-4 genuine address spellings fail, rule out context with WIDE probes (end and top/before), then align other blocks of the same function to the target's shape (switch/if-chain, block order) and re-check the early SIB.
rules.not_when: Narrow count probes (e.g. 0-2) prove nothing; if a wide end probe flips it, treat it as back-end TU context instead.

evidence.counts: CEvent::TreatEventBase +0xAC SIB matched after the Escape handling took the target if-chain shape; identical prefix 172 -> 730 bytes; context probes negative over the ranges above

rules.keywords: sib base index swap register allocation function-wide switch if-chain shape

rules.title: Commuted SIB residues are not explained by the VC5 compiler build
rules.symptom: Same effective address with SIB base/index commuted; spellings and context probes did not flip it.
rules.construct: (none - negative result)
rules.explanation: Compiling the same event.cpp candidate with all seven local VC5 trees (SP3, SP2, RTM, NT5 1592, NT5 1691, SP3 DEU, SP3 JPN) produced identical bytes at both SIB sites (ChangeButtons +0x5fb 8a 54 0e 25 vs target 8a 54 31 25; TreatEventBase old/new forms) and changed none of 50 accepted event functions.
rules.experiment: Do not spend compiles on compiler-tree sweeps for SIB order; look for source/control-flow shape (BLUPI-REG-01) instead.
rules.not_when: Other residue classes (e.g. the two sound helpers where RTM differs, BLUPI-FLG-01) can be build-sensitive.

evidence.counts: 7 compiler trees x 3 function forms; 0/50 accepted functions changed

rules.keywords: sib commuted compiler build sp2 sp3 rtm nt5 sweep negative

blupi_evidence.outcome: negative: no tree flips the SIB

rules.title: SIB base/index order follows the identity of the index variable (shared vs separate locals)
rules.symptom: Same effective address, base and index commuted (e.g. 8a 54 0e 25 vs 8a 54 31 25); address spellings, context probes and compiler builds do not change it.
rules.construct: Whether two loops/blocks reuse ONE index local or use separate locals for the same role.
rules.explanation: VC5 SP3 /O2: the choice of base vs index register for [reg+reg+disp] followed which variable supplied the index; reusing a single player-index local (as the original did) reproduced the target order, separate locals commuted it. Lexical scope and the count of unused locals alone did not matter. Reproduced in a 112-byte micro TU.
rules.experiment: For each commuted SIB, identify the index variable; try merging same-role index locals into one (or splitting a shared one) and recompile; confirm in a micro TU when unsure.
rules.not_when: If wide context probes flip it, treat it as TU context; if a later block's control-flow shape flips it, see BLUPI-REG-01.

evidence.counts: CEvent::ChangeButtons 0x1b220 became STRICT (2,854 B, 83 relocations) after sharing one player-index local; 112-byte micro reproduction; TreatEventBase: 36 variants show index identity matters, scope/unused locals do not

rules.keywords: sib base index commuted shared local index variable identity loop

rules.title: An unused anonymous-union type in a shared class header shifts VC5 TU context
rules.symptom: A correct member-layout change in a shared header regresses an unrelated accepted function in another TU, although the scalar member count did not change.
rules.construct: Extra or missing type declarations inside the class (anonymous unions, nested structs) rather than plain members.
rules.explanation: In SB1, the SB2-derived decor.h carried an unused anonymous union (moveObjectSpeed). Its type declaration consumed VC5 symbol-counter numbers in every including TU; with it present the recovered CDecor layout regressed CButton::MouseMove (button.cpp), with it removed MouseMove stayed STRICT and CDecor::BlupiStep (25,269 B) became STRICT. Scalar member count alone did not explain the shift.
rules.experiment: When a layout fix regresses another TU, diff the two headers in counter terms (types, unions, nested structs, declarators), remove declarations the original did not have, and re-run the whole-tree gate.
rules.not_when: Do not remove a union/type that oracle code actually uses; never add filler to compensate.

evidence.counts: whole tree 324/324 accepted pass; BlupiStep 117 fixed differences -> 0, 350 relocations

rules.keywords: anonymous union nested type declaration header context shift layout regression
